$comment: SCHEMA PROBE, not a run. Hand-filled for app/account/activate to give template.schema.json its first contact with real data. Originally used semantic tpl ids and was migrated to D13's positional rule -- which means it no longer resolves the three ids F7 pre-registered: the baseline cites tpl:if-success, this defines tpl:1, and under D13 the baseline's names are unreproducible and stay unresolved permanently.

ast.$comment_empty: Eleven of the eighteen node kinds are empty for this component. That is the honest shape of a passive screen -- no bindings, no events, no interpolation, no child components. An extractor that omitted empty arrays instead of emitting them would make 'no event handlers' indistinguishable from 'events not extracted'.

accessibility.$comment: Carries presentational alert styling but no role and no live-region attribute, so assistive technology is not told the outcome.

ast.$comment_ids: Ids are 0-based document order by source start offset (D13). Migrated from the semantic names this probe originally used -- tpl:if-success became tpl:1 -- because no parser reproduces a name the template never gave. Read loc, not the id, to locate a node.

uiRequirements.statement: The screen shows a centred column containing a heading and, at most, one status message. There is no other content.
A success message is shown only once a key has been redeemed successfully.
A failure message is shown only once a redemption attempt has failed.
The two conditions are independent, so nothing prevents both messages from being shown at once.
While the server is being contacted, neither message is shown and only the heading appears. There is no pending indication.
A link to the sign-in screen is offered inside the success message, and only there.
All four visible strings are translation keys resolved at display time; the embedded English is fallback copy.
Status messages carry alert styling but no announcement role, so assistive technology is not explicitly told the outcome.

warnings: Schema probe, not extractor output. Determinism is not claimed.
No test exercises this template -- the spec replaces it with an empty string -- so every statement here is uncorroborated by tests.
